sol_answer.answer: The formula uses ischemic stroke as reference and unequal weights for the other outcomes, rather than a deduplicated first-event composite.

sonnet_answer.answer: The records state that sources use different composites and weights. ASPREE MACE excludes bleeding, ASCEND includes TIA, one meta-analysis weights hemorrhagic stroke 3x ischemic stroke, and the USPSTF model uses lifetime QALYs. No record demonstrates that the sign of the net effect reverses under alternative definitions or weights, so the claim's dependence is inferred from heterogeneity of definitions, not shown directly.

evidence.text: The commissioned model combined nonfatal cardiovascular benefits and gastrointestinal and intracranial bleeding harms into lifetime QALYs and life-years, assuming no cardiovascular mortality effect. For initiation at ages 60–69, QALY gains ranged from slightly negative to slightly positive by cardiovascular risk and life-year gains were generally negative; at ages 70–79, both measures were negative at essentially all modeled risks up to 20% ten-year cardiovascular risk. These lifetime modeled endpoints do not determine the specified five-year, equally weighted first-event composite.
evidence.quote: Initiation of aspirin use in persons aged 60 to 69 years results in quality-adjusted life-years gained that range from slightly negative to slightly positive depending on CVD risk level, and life-years gained are generally negative.
